arxiv-1806-01275.title: Modeling noise and error correction for Majorana-based quantum computing
arxiv-1806-01275.creator: Christina Knapp, Michael Beverland, Dmitry I. Pikulin, Torsten Karzig
arxiv-1806-01275.description: Abstract Majorana-based quantum computing seeks to use the non-local nature of Majorana zero modes to store and manipulate quantum information in a topologically protected way. While noise is anticipated to be significantly suppressed in such systems, finite temperature and system size result in residual errors.

arxiv-2111-02317.title: Smells in System User Interactive Tests
arxiv-2111-02317.creator: Renaud Rwemalika, Sarra Habchi, Mike Papadakis, Yves Le Traon, Marie-Claude Brasseur
arxiv-2111-02317.description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by Renaud Rwemalika, Sarra Habchi, Mike Papadakis, Yves Le Traon, Marie-Claude Brasseur. ∎

Abstract

Test smells are known as bad development practices that reflect poor design and implementation choices in software tests. Over the last decade, test smells were heavily studied to measure their prevalence and impacts on test maintainability. However, these studies focused mainly on the unit level and to this day, the work on system tests that interact with the System Under Test through a Graphical User Interface remains limited.

arxiv-2205-07783.title: Strong Equivalence of Logic Programs with Counting
arxiv-2205-07783.creator: Vladimir Lifschitz
arxiv-2205-07783.description: Abstract In answer set programming, two groups of rules are considered strongly equivalent if they have the same meaning in any context. In some cases, strong equivalence of programs in the input language of the grounder gringo can be established by deriving rules of each program from rules of the other.

arxiv-2209-09734.title: Phase Randomness in a Semiconductor Laser: the Issue of Quantum Random Number Generation
arxiv-2209-09734.creator: Roman Shakhovoy, Marius Puplauskis, Violetta Sharoglazova, Alexander Duplinskiy, Denis Sych, Elizaveta Maksimova, Selbi Hydyrova, Alexander Tumachek, Yury Mironov, Vadim Kovalyuk, Alexey Prokhodtsov, Grigory Goltsman, Yury Kurochkin
arxiv-2209-09734.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Roman Shakhovoy, Marius Puplauskis, Violetta Sharoglazova, Alexander Duplinskiy, Denis Sych, Elizaveta Maksimova, Selbi Hydyrova, Alexander Tumachek, Yury Mironov, Vadim Kovalyuk, Alexey Prokhodtsov, Grigory Goltsman, Yury Kurochkin. Gain-switched lasers are in demand in numerous quantum applications, particularly, in systems of quantum key distribution and in various optical quantum random number generators. The reason for this popularity is natural phase randomization between gain-switched laser pulses.

arxiv-2308-16341.title: Triple Points of Gravitational AdS Solitons and Black Holes
arxiv-2308-16341.creator: Constanza Quijada, Andrés Anabalón, Robert B. Mann, Julio Oliva
arxiv-2308-16341.description: Abstract Résumé We present a triple point of a new kind for General Relativity, at which two gravitational solitons can coexist with a planar black hole in anti de Sitter space. Working in the context of non-linear electrodynamics, we obtain simple, sensible spacetimes for which the thermodynamics can be studied in an analytic manner.

arxiv-2402-01898.title: Search for long-lived particles decaying in the CMS muon detectors in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
arxiv-2402-01898.description: Abstract A search for long-lived particles (LLPs) decaying in the CMS muon detectors is presented. A data sample of proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 \fbinv , recorded at the LHC in 2016–2018, is used.

arxiv-2501-06228.title: Identifying Electronic Doorway States in the Secondary Electron Emission from Layered Materials
arxiv-2501-06228.creator: A. Niggas, M. Hao, P. Richter, F. Simperl, F. Blödorn, M. Cap, J. Kero, D. Hofmann, A. Bellissimo, J. Burgdörfer, T. Seyller, R.A. Wilhelm, F. Libisch, W.S.M. Werner
arxiv-2501-06228.description: Abstract We investigate the secondary low-energy electron emission induced by inelastic electron scattering from graphene and layered materials thereof. By applying a coincidence detection of the primary scattered and the emitted secondary electron we unravel pronounced resonance features otherwise overshadowed by the largely structureless secondary electron energy distribution.

arxiv-2507-13178.description: Abstract We study randomized generation of sequences of test-inputs to a system using Prolog. pmc-11313899.title: Corrosion and Interfacial Contact Resistance of NiTi Alloy as a Promising Bipolar Plate for PEMFC
pmc-11313899.creator: Yingping Li, Xiaofen Wang, Yuanyuan Li, Zhuo He, Guohong Zhang, Zhen Wang, Shaohua Wang, Fei Hu, Qiongyu Zhou
pmc-11313899.description: Titanium (Ti) is generally considered as an ideal bipolar plate (BPP) material because of its excellent corrosion resistance, good machinability and lightweight nature. pmc-11396632.title: Permethrin exposure primes neuroinflammatory stress response to drive depression-like behavior through microglial activation in a mouse model of Gulf War Illness
pmc-11396632.creator: Sean X. Naughton, Eun-Jeong Yang, Umar Iqbal, Kyle Trageser, Daniel Charytonowicz, Sibilla Masieri, Molly Estill, Henry Wu, Urdhva Raval, Weiting Lyu, Qing-li Wu, Li Shen, James Simon, Robert Sebra, Giulio Maria Pasinetti
pmc-11396632.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Gulf War Illness (GWI) is a chronic multisymptom disorder that affects approximately 25–32% of Gulf War veterans and is characterized by a number of symptoms such as cognitive impairment, psychiatric disturbances, chronic fatigue and gastrointestinal distress, among others. While the exact etiology of GWI is unknown, it is believed to have been caused by toxic exposures encountered during deployment in combination with other factors such as stress.

pmc-11584938.title: Ureaplasma urealyticum pyelonephritis associated with renal, perinephric, retroperitoneal, and bladder abscesses in a hypogammaglobinemic adult patient presenting with gross hematuria and marked thrombocytosis

pmc-11584938.description: Ureaplasma urealyticum is an opportunistic bacterium that is often identified in asymptomatic, healthy individuals from colonization of the genitourinary tract. However, in immunocompromised patients with hypogammaglobulinemia, Ureaplasma has been reported to cause a wide range of infections, most commonly urethritis and cystitis.

This prospective study evaluated treatment outcomes in 432 adult patients with chronic hepatitis C (CHC) treated with direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) at the University Clinical Center of Serbia.

pmc-12816087.title: Slower-growing species promote interspecific cooperation and coexistence under acid stress through cross-feeding
pmc-12816087.creator: Hui Liao, Liming Wu, Yi Luo, Hussain Asif, Xinlei Huang, Xiaole Xia
pmc-12816087.description: Acid stress is a central environmental factor shaping the structure and function of microbial communities worldwide. However, there is a lack of predictive understanding of how microbial communities respond physiologically and metabolically to acid stress. Here, we find that higher acid stress favors slower-growing species, promoting population growth and coexistence.

pmc-13045154.creator: Florence Carrouel, Rita Nugem, Yohan Fayet, Laurie Fraticelli, Lama Basbous, Jean-Francois Vian, Camille Vindras, Corélie Salque, Claude Dussart, Marie-Thérèse Charreyre, Romain Lan, Audrey Murat-Ringot
pmc-13045154.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe Planetary Health Diet (PHD), developed by the EAT–Lancet Commission, provides a comprehensive framework to promote human and planetary health through dietary transformation. Despite its benefits, adoption of the PHD remains limited in high-income countries like France. This study aimed to evaluate knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors (KAB) related to the PHD across diverse French populations and identify determinants of inadequate KAB.MethodsThis cross-sectional quantitative study was conducted between April and June 2024 under the BIOQUALIM protocol.

pmc-13310157.title: Arterial Stiffness as a Predictor of Postoperative Intensive Care Unit (ICU) Mortality: An Observational Study
pmc-13310157.creator: Panagiota Gatsori, George Intas, Theodoros A Katsoulas, Eleni Theodosopoulou, Dimitrios Cholevas, Ilias Skopelitis, Pantelis I Stergiannis
pmc-13310157.description: BackgroundArterial stiffness has emerged as a key determinant of cardiovascular risk, yet its prognostic impact in postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) patients remains unclear. This study evaluated the association of arterial stiffness indices (augmentation index (AIX@75), pulse pressure (PP)) with ICU mortality in postoperative surgical patients.MethodsThis was a prospective observational study including 117 postoperative ICU patients.

pmc-13369144.title: Design and implementation of a hybrid machine learning framework for predicting heart rate status
pmc-13369144.creator: Mahsa Emami, Neda Salehbagheri, Saman Rajebi, Siamak Pedrammehr, Kimia Shirini
pmc-13369144.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Real-time accurate evaluation of heart rate status during physical activity is a critical requirement in physiological analysis, performance enhancement, and early warning systems for cardiovascular diseases. In this work, a lightweight hybrid machine learning model for classifying the status of heart rate during physical activities into normal and warning levels using a combination strategy of Multilayer Perceptron, Naïve Bayes, and K-Nearest Neighbors algorithms in a weighted voting–based ensemble model is presented.

pmc-13414985.title: Inflammatory-neurological deficit versus metabolic dysregulation: unsupervised clustering and SHAP analysis
